rationale: Counterfactual campaign tests causal necessity of Blackboard/DAG state in the heterogeneous (Arm C) architecture. Arm A (monolithic Parrot) has no Blackboard or internal DAG, so poison/remove operations are meaningless. Arm B (Parrot-centric DAG) is a bridge architecture; counterfactual experiments on it risk confusing the heterogeneity analysis by mixing architectural effects with causal effects. Arm C represents the full heterogeneous system where Blackboard state, node dependencies, and DAG routing are all present and causal.
what_is_counterfactual: Two integrity tests: (1) POISON: flip a discovered fact on the Blackboard (e.g., change a reading from 60 to 61, or a verification status from VERIFIED to UNSUPPORTED); verify that downstream nodes notice and terminal output changes. (2) REMOVE: delete a node from the DAG (or its output from Blackboard); verify that the run fails or produces a different output (or explicit MISSING_DEPENDENCY error).
why_arm_c_only: Arm C's heterogeneous composition depends on coordinated node state on the Blackboard. Causal necessity tests must perturb that state.
Arm A has no Blackboard; perturbation has nowhere to go.
Arm B has a Blackboard but it is the 'bridge' arm, mixing monolithic-Parrot cognition (via adapters) with shallow internal DAG structure. Confounding risk is high.
Arm C is the scientific target: do heterogeneous microservices really work better? Counterfactuals on Arm C directly test whether coordination and state-sharing are necessary.

ARM_A.detail: No internal DAG nodes; no Blackboard coordination. Poison/remove experiments undefined.

ARM_B.detail: Mixes Parrot cognition with local DAG structure. Unclear whether effects come from heterogeneity or from Parrot's inherent properties.

counterfactual_manifest_specification.structure: One workflow per primary example, modified for Arm C only
poison_operations: Replace a reading (e.g., A from 60 to 61)
Flip a verification status (VERIFIED -> UNSUPPORTED, or vice versa)
Negate an intermediate result (e.g., diff from 100 to -100)
remove_operations: Delete a node from the DAG (e.g., remove NORMALIZE step)
Delete a Blackboard entry (Observation or Fact)
Simulate missing dependency (e.g., marked as MISSING_DEPENDENCY)

expected_outcomes.poison_test: If causal necessity holds, terminal output or verification status should differ from primary
expected_outcomes.remove_test: If causal necessity holds, run should fail with dependency error or produce a different output

recording_and_analysis.counterfactual_results: Recorded in Section-7 analysis as integrity-test-passing (did perturbation cause expected change?) vs integrity-test-failing (did not change or changed unexpectedly)
recording_and_analysis.threshold: Arm C counterfactual passing rate >= 95% qualifies as 'causal necessity confirmed' (with caveats)

scope_enforcement.implementation: Counterfactual runner loops only over workflows tagged with arm='C'
scope_enforcement.error_on_other_arms: If a counterfactual configuration names Arm A or B, runner logs CONFIGURATION_ERROR and skips
scope_enforcement.no_mixed_runs: Never run the same counterfactual (same poison/remove spec) against multiple arms in one experiment
